name: AGH University of Krakow
summary: Kraków technical university of about 21,000 students; seven English bachelor's in computing, physics, geology, mechanics and space.

ib.text: Ranked on IB grades: maths (SL, or HL) x2 plus your best two listed HL subjects x6 and x2, each rescaled to 30-100, out of 1000; 300 needed. With an IB you skip AGH's maths exam.

lastYear.text: 1 June–9 July (10 am CEST); later cycles if places remain

programmes.name: Computer Physics
programmes.about: Physics and mathematics combined with computational methods: modelling, simulation and data analysis of physical and engineering problems, at the Faculty of Physics and Applied Computer Science.
programmes.overview: The first two years pair mathematical analysis, algebra, mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum and statistical physics with programming, algorithms, Unix, object-oriented programming and numerical methods. Teaching mixes lectures, problem-solving classes, laboratories and workshops, and you are assessed through exams and projects. Electives let you lean towards artificial intelligence and machine learning, data science, GPU computing, digital systems or scientific computing. Graduates go into research institutes, engineering firms, high-performance computing centres and industrial R&D, or on to a master's in a physics-related field such as Technical Physics.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: Building and using computer systems: maths and physics foundations, programming, PC and mobile systems, administration and data analysis, run by four AGH faculties together.
programmes.overview: The first year builds the mathematical base (analysis, algebra, discrete mathematics, logic, statistics) alongside introductory computer science, Unix, two programming courses and physics. Lectures are joined by laboratory and project classes, and later years add elective groups such as semantic web, process mining, programming language theory, constraint and logic programming. The course includes a required internship in semester 6 and a capstone project in semester 7, and a business analysis information systems option is available. It prepares engineers for software development, systems administration, data analysis and the design of PC and mobile systems.

programmes.name: Computer Science for Embedded Systems
programmes.about: Designing embedded systems like those in cars, robots, IoT devices and medical equipment, from hardware to software, with lab work, team projects and simulation and testing tools.
programmes.overview: You start with algebra, mathematical analysis, programming, operating systems administration, data transmission, microcontroller basics and digital electronics, then move on to algorithms, object-oriented and functional programming, physics and metrology. Classes combine lectures, laboratories, workshops and project work. Instead of fixed tracks, electives in the later years cover low-level and high-level programming, real-time operating systems, FPGA and GPU acceleration, system security, signal processing, embedded AI and wireless systems. Graduates work on embedded design in sectors such as automotive, robotics, IoT and medical devices, or continue to a second-cycle degree.

programmes.name: Geology of Natural Resources
programmes.about: Finding and assessing mineral deposits for the energy transition and critical raw materials: geochemistry, geophysics, GIS and data modelling, with lab and field classes.
programmes.overview: The first year covers mathematics for geologists, chemistry, physical geology, mineralogy and petrology, physics in geology, statistics and geostatistics, GIS, environmental assessment and computational geoscience. Fieldwork is a large part of the course, with 90 hours of field courses in year one and 60 in year two, plus lab classes, projects, an internship and a seminar leading to a diploma project. In the final years you choose pathways such as geoenergy resources, mining hydrogeology, geomaterials, remote sensing, renewables and the energy transition, or computational deposit analysis. Graduates enter the raw materials industry, mineral exploration, mining companies, research, consultancy and public administration.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Designing mechanical systems: materials, strength, corrosion and manufacturing technology, at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Robotics.
programmes.overview: Year one lays the groundwork with mathematics, physics, chemistry, information technology, manufacturing processes, engineering drawing, fundamentals of mechanical engineering and materials science. Teaching combines lectures, laboratories, seminars and project classes where you learn design and CAD, and a practical placement comes in the final year. For the diploma you choose one of nine profiles, for example ropeway transport systems, earthmoving and heavy-duty machinery, energy technologies, manufacturing process engineering, advanced design methods or ecological systems engineering. Graduates design mechanical systems, and the programme reports that most find work within months, at firms such as Valeo, Delphi and ABB.

programmes.name: Mechatronic Engineering
programmes.about: Mechanics, control, electronics and computing brought together: computer-aided engineering, virtual prototyping, modern control and the basics of robotics.
programmes.overview: The first year covers algebra, analysis, physics, chemistry, programming and the basics of informatics, followed in year two by mechanics, strength of materials, engineering drawing, signals and systems, numerical methods, manufacturing technology, and electronics and electrical engineering. Lectures are combined with auditorium, laboratory and project classes and seminars. Later optional modules let you focus on robotics (industrial or service robots), intelligent methods such as deep learning or vision, signal processing, and object-oriented or microcontroller programming. Graduates work in design offices, R&D institutions and companies that make or use mechatronic devices, or continue to a master's in Poland or abroad.

programmes.name: Space Engineering
programmes.about: Designing, integrating and operating space systems: spacecraft and satellites, propulsion, avionics, flight dynamics and ground segment, in design studios and mission projects with an internship.
programmes.overview: The opening year combines calculus, algebra, physics, engineering mechanics, materials science and chemistry with programming, electronics, engineering design and CAD. The emphasis is hands-on: laboratories, design studios, system integration workshops and multi-stage engineering projects modelled on real missions, plus an obligatory industry or research internship. Electives in later years cover spacecraft subsystems (avionics, power and thermal, propulsion), space systems engineering, Earth observation, space robotics and rovers, mission cybersecurity, space economy and policy, and bioastronautics. Graduates move into spacecraft and satellite engineering, mission operations, avionics and control, space software and data engineering, or on to a master's in a space-related field.

notes: Without Polish citizenship you apply through AGH's international recruitment and pay the programme fee; EU citizens get no lower rate.
With an IB diploma you need no apostille or NAWA statement, and as an EU citizen at a school in the EU or OECD no English certificate.
You apply after your IB exams and type your IB grades into e-Rekrutacja yourself; the diploma scan goes in with them.
